findings.issue: Test evidence records commit e722562 but HEAD is d1aa0a3, so it does not describe the tree being released. The recorded run is not wrong about the code it measured: e722562 to 1beea8b differs only in governance JSON, and d1aa0a3 touches no app, components, convex or lib file. But the requirement is commit === HEAD. The self-referential trap is the root cause: evidence must record the commit it ran against, and evidence is itself committed, so a record inside a commit can never equal that commit's SHA. Re-running the same sequence moves HEAD again and stays stale. Settle it in the recording template: either record HEAD after the artefacts are committed and accept a documented follow-up commit, or record HEAD at run start with a tree hash a reviewer can verify is unchanged.

NFR-008's 500-item sync budget has no measuring evidence. The read paths pass with wide margins, but the write path swings from 3.51 s (pass) to 5.01 s and 10.30 s (fail) at 3,500 rows, and 14.87 s to 21.19 s at 15,000 rows, all with a byte-identical batch argument. That variance exceeds the margin to the 5 s budget, so no verdict can be read from it in either direction. The handler does one indexed .unique() per item and one patch, so no missing index explains it; the untested explanation is the in-memory convex-test simulation.
NFR-009 has no accessibility evidence. No axe pass ran over the feature surfaces, so the WCAG 2.1 AA claim rests only on unit-level screen assertions.
